To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed 3D face recognition system based on the use of the HK algorithm for region segmentation, the use of the selected 3D geometrical features, and the matching scheme based on SVM, is a promising system for 3D face identification.
1) 3D face recognition using 3-D geometrical features is a feasible approach, and 2) 3D geometrical features can be used to achieve a high performance of face recognition.

3D face recognition using local geometrical features can achieve a high level of accuracy under controlled conditions and that the recognition rate is still acceptable under non-controlled conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective face recognition system using 3D facial meshes.
the extraction of the most discriminating features from 3D faces.
3D face modeling and recognition using local geometrical features, with the purpose to improve the robustness of face recognition algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SVM matching scheme is the most robust one for face recognition under controlled and non controlled acquisition conditions.
the use of 3D local geometry is a good choice to model faces.
the use of 3D geometrical features is a very promising approach in face recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the SVM algorithm is a more suitable choice than PCA for the face recognition task, and that the use of 3D local geometry features is a good alternative to texture-based approaches.
the 3D local features are robust to facial expression and rotation.
the SVM is the best matching scheme for the selected features, and that the selected features can be used for face recognition under non-controlled conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3D face recognition is a viable alternative for biometrics, and it is not necessary to use expensive and complex equipment to obtain the 3D facial meshes.

local geometrical features are robust for face recognition under controlled conditions and, to a lesser extent, under non-controlled conditions, and that the SVM matching scheme is more efficient than PCA.
local geometrical features are very discriminant to model the face and to achieve robust face recognition.
